findings.issue_text: [High/bug] apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx (~line 45): zod formSchema passed to zodResolver was not updated with the new backupCode field, so zod strips the unknown key and backupCode never reaches signIn("credentials", ...), breaking backup-code login from the login page; fix by adding backupCode: z.string().optional() to formSchema

[Medium/concurrency] packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131-155: backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt → indexOf → null out → re-encrypt → prisma.user.update) with no transaction or optimistic locking, so two concurrent sign-ins with the same code can both succeed (single-use violated) and concurrent use of two different codes can lose an update and resurrect a consumed code

[Medium/bug] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:222-232: at SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes the Cancel button is hidden and dismissing via Esc/overlay/X (onOpenChange) calls neither onEnable() nor resetState(), so the parent is never notified that 2FA was enabled and the modal's internal step stays on the backup-codes screen for the next open

[Medium/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts: no e2e coverage for the core new behaviors — logging in with a backup code, single-use enforcement (reused code must be rejected), and disabling 2FA with a backup code; existing assertions only exercise download/copy/close UI

[Low/security] packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:148 and apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:57: backup codes are compared with Array.indexOf/plain string equality (non-constant-time), a timing side channel for secret verification; use a constant-time comparison such as crypto.timingSafeEqual

[Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:55 and packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:140: JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...)) is unguarded, so corrupt/undecryptable stored data (e.g., after an encryption-key rotation) throws an unhandled exception producing a 500/authorize crash instead of a clean error response

[Low/bug] apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx:7: the component is defined and exported as TwoFactor (copy-paste from TwoFactor.tsx), so React devtools, error stack traces, and future maintenance reference the wrong component for the backup-code input

[Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:57 and next-auth-options.ts:148: the submitted code is only dash-stripped with no trim() or case normalization, so input with stray whitespace or uppercase hex is rejected as 'incorrect backup code' even when the user copied a valid code

[Low/bug] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:74-79: resetState() clears only password/error/step while backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, dataUri, secret, and the form's totpCode survive cancel/reopen, and the blob object URL is never revoked when the modal closes (leak plus stale secrets held in memory)

[Low/bug] packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:47-53: adding tabIndex={-1} to the password-visibility toggle removes it from keyboard tab order, so keyboard users can no longer toggle password visibility (a11y regression in a shared UI component)

[Low/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:50-51: expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy() asserts on a Promise object which is always truthy, making the check a no-op; the PR only adds a FIXME comment instead of fixing the assertion (e.g., await expect(locator).toBeChecked())

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:222-232: at SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes the Cancel button is hidden and dismissing via Esc/overlay/X (onOpenChange) calls neither onEnable() nor resetState(), so the parent is never notified that 2FA was enabled and the modal's internal step stays on the backup-codes screen for the next open

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, a successful enable transitions to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` (`handleEnable` setsStep instead of calling `onEnable()`). At that step, the Cancel button is explicitly not rendered (`step !== SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes ? <Button ...>cancel</Button> : null`). The only place that calls both `resetState()` and `onEnable()` at this step is the “close” button handler (`data-testid="backup-codes-close"`). The `Dialog`’s `onOpenChange` is just passed through from props and there is no handler here to invoke `resetState()`/`onEnable()` on dismiss via Esc/overlay/X, so if the parent closes the modal that way, this component’s internal `step` remains `DisplayBackupCodes` for the next open and the parent is not notified via `onEnable()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts: no e2e coverage for the core new behaviors — logging in with a backup code, single-use enforcement (reused code must be rejected), and disabling 2FA with a backup code; existing assertions only exercise download/copy/close UI

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new backup-code flows (login UI toggle in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx`, credential verification + single-use deletion in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, and disabling 2FA via backup code in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx`). The updated Playwright test `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` only adds UI checks for the post-enable backup-code dialog (download/copy/close) and even contains a `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup` comment, with no coverage for (a) logging in using a backup code, (b) verifying single-use enforcement (reusing a code should fail), or (c) disabling 2FA using a backup code. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/security] packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:148 and apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:57: backup codes are compared with Array.indexOf/plain string equality (non-constant-time), a timing side channel for secret verification; use a constant-time comparison such as crypto.timingSafeEqual

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows backup code verification implemented via `backupCodes.indexOf(userInput)` in both `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (e.g., `const index = backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""));`) and `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (e.g., `const index = backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""));`). This relies on plain string equality during search, which is not constant-time and can theoretically leak information via timing differences when verifying a secret. Using a constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual`) would mitigate this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:55 and packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:140: JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...)) is unguarded, so corrupt/undecryptable stored data (e.g., after an encryption-key rotation) throws an unhandled exception producing a 500/authorize crash instead of a clean error response

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds backup-code handling that does `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY))` in both `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` without any try/catch or validation. If `user.backupCodes` is corrupted or undecryptable (e.g., key rotation or bad data), `symmetricDecrypt` and/or `JSON.parse` can throw, leading to an unhandled exception (500 in the API route; thrown error in `authorize` that can crash/return generic server error) instead of a controlled error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:47-53: adding tabIndex={-1} to the password-visibility toggle removes it from keyboard tab order, so keyboard users can no longer toggle password visibility (a11y regression in a shared UI component)

adjudication.rationale: In packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx, the password visibility toggle is a <button type="button">. The diff adds tabIndex={-1} to that button, which removes it from the normal keyboard tab order. That makes the toggle unreachable via Tab navigation for keyboard-only users, causing an accessibility regression in a shared UI component.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:50-51: expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy() asserts on a Promise object which is always truthy, making the check a no-op; the PR only adds a FIXME comment instead of fixing the assertion (e.g., await expect(locator).toBeChecked())

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts the code `await expect(page.locator(`[data-testid=two-factor-switch]`).isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` is asserting on the Promise returned by `locator.isChecked()`, not on a resolved boolean. A Promise object is always truthy, so the assertion is effectively a no-op (the newly added FIXME comment even notes this). The diff does not fix the assertion to something like `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()` or `expect(await locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()`.
